_about: Tabla data for bandbox: talas (rhythm cycles), and what each bol (spoken stroke syllable) plays. Data, not code: correct it here. Not yet checked by a tabla player; corrections welcome.
_talas: beats = matras in one cycle (avartan). vibhag = the cycle's sections. marks = the clap sign at the start of each vibhag: X = sam (the first beat, clapped), a number = tali (clapped), 0 = khali (a wave, empty). theka = the standard basic bols of the cycle, '|' between vibhags.

teentaal.theka: dha dhin dhin dha | dha dhin dhin dha | dha tin tin ta | ta dhin dhin dha
teentaal.about: Teentaal (tintal, trital): 16 beats, 4+4+4+4, the most common tala in Hindustani music. The third vibhag is khali: after its first beat the bayan drops out (dhin becomes tin). Some teachers write that vibhag na tin tin ta.

keherwa.theka: dha ge na ti | na ka dhi na
keherwa.about: Keherwa: 8 beats, 4+4. Light classical, film and folk songs.

dadra.theka: dha dhi na | dha tu na
dadra.about: Dadra: 6 beats, 3+3. Light classical (dadra, ghazal, bhajan).

rupak._marks: conventions vary: some books number rupak's talis 2 and 3
rupak.theka: tin tin na | dhi na | dhi na
rupak.about: Rupak: 7 beats, 3+2+2. Unusual in starting on khali: its first beat (sam) is a wave, not a clap.

_strokes: The seven sounds bandbox has a sample for. bayan = the left-hand bass drum, dayan = the right-hand treble drum. damps = a closed stroke that stops the same drum's ringing; open strokes ring on into each other. gain = level against the loudest stroke (the samples are all normalised).

ke.about: closed, flat-hand bass slap (ka, ki, kat)

tin.about: open stroke on the edge of the black spot, ringing

tun.about: open stroke in the centre, long ring (tu)

te.about: closed centre stroke, dry (ti, the ti in tirakita)

re.about: closed stroke with the other fingers, dry (ra)

_bols: Each bol plays one stroke, or a bayan and a dayan stroke together.
_compounds: Bols spoken as one word that are played as several quick strokes, sharing their beat evenly.
